strategy_plan.planning_summary: The problem requires optimizing a fixed two-layer topology (one SiO2, one TiO2) on glass to minimize mean reflectance over 450-700 nm. Since the material set is restricted to exactly two specific oxides and the layer count is fixed at two, the only distinct strategic axes are the two possible permutations of the layer order: Air/SiO2/TiO2/Glass versus Air/TiO2/SiO2/Glass. These represent fundamentally different impedance matching profiles (graded index vs. high-index step). Given the constraint of maximum 1 route, the priority axis is the theoretically superior graded-index approach (Low-n then High-n), which typically offers broader bandwidth antireflection properties for this specific substrate index. This single route will tune both layer thicknesses within the specified bounds to find the global minimum for that specific ordering.

routes.title: Optimization of Low-High Index Two-Layer AR Coating
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A two-layer stack with the low-index material (SiO2) adjacent to air and the high-index material (TiO2) adjacent to the glass substrate will achieve a lower arithmetic mean reflectance across the 450-700 nm band than the reverse ordering, given the thickness constraints of 40-160 nm.
routes.design_principle: Impedance matching theory suggests that stepping the refractive index from air (1.0) to substrate (1.52) via an intermediate low index (1.46) then high index (2.40) creates a smoother effective index gradient than starting with a high index jump, potentially reducing Fresnel reflections over a wider spectral range.

# TMM research and design result

Run status: completed. Acceptance: accepted.

## Problem interpretation

Design a planar two-layer antireflection coating on a semi-infinite glass substrate (refractive index 1.52, lossless) with air incidence (refractive index 1.0). The design must use exactly one layer of lossless SiO2 (n=1.46) and one layer of lossless TiO2 (n=2.40) in either order. Each layer thickness is constrained between 40 nm and 160 nm. The objective is to minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance for s-polarized light at normal incidence, sampled from 450 nm to 700 nm in 5 nm steps. The stated performance target is a mean reflectance below 0.03. The method must use deterministic Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) only. The optimization allows at most two research rounds with one route and up to 64 solver evaluations per round using seed 17. Decisions to adjust or stop must be based on observed results and independent numeric checks.

- No reusable literature method was available; planning used explicit optical theory assumptions.
